diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since \(\operatorname{supp}\{U^n_i\} = \Omega_i\), it further follows that \(U^n_i \in H_0(\Omega_i)\).

issues.failure_explanation: The defined space uses strict compact support (subset subset), but the paper repeatedly assumes functions with support equal to the whole element/domain and then claims membership in H_0. For L^2 functions this set is not closed, so the stated Hilbert-space claim is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the compact-support condition by support in Ω (zero-extended L^2(Ω) functions), or otherwise redefine H_0 consistently with the later usage.
issues.overall_effect: All results asserting membership in H_0(Ω), H_0(Ω_i), or H_0(Ω~) are unreliable under the stated definition.
issues.title: H_0 definition is incompatible with its L^2 usage and is not complete
issues.why_classification: A local definitional correction preserves the intended L^2 framework and all substantive claims without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \(\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d\) be a bounded domain, and assume \(\operatorname{supp}\{\Psi(x)\} = \Omega\).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof infers Ψ(y)≠0 from y∈supp{Ψ}. For L^2 data (or even continuous data on the boundary of the support) a support point need not be a point of nonvanishing, so the inclusion argument is not valid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the lemma in terms of essential support and use the standard measure-theoretic argument under the characteristic flow.
issues.overall_effect: The support identity used to localize the integral invariant in the existence proof is unsupported.
issues.title: Support lemma proof invalidly equates support membership with pointwise nonzero values
issues.why_classification: The conclusion can be preserved by a local proof repair using essential support; no change to the main scheme is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that once \(t_1\) and \(t_2\) are fixed, \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau\) is a constant.

issues.failure_explanation: The map x ↦ x + ∫ A(s(τ),τ)dτ is the characteristic flow, not a translation. Its Jacobian is generally not 1 unless div A=0, which is not assumed. For example, in 1D with A(x)=x the L^P norm of Ψ(flow(x)) is not preserved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false norm-invariance lemmas by inequalities involving the flow Jacobian, or add a divergence-free hypothesis; then carry the resulting constants through the stability proof.
issues.overall_effect: The stability induction and the uniqueness argument, which use ||ψ||=||Ψ|| at each step, are unsupported; the claimed constants C_k are not justified.
issues.title: Characteristic flow is incorrectly treated as norm-preserving
issues.why_classification: A contained correction to the change-of-variables estimates can preserve the unconditional stability theorem with a different constant, but the source does not provide that estimate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: V(\mathbf{x}; W, \mathbf{A}, t_p, \Delta t) = W\left(\mathbf{x} + \int_{t_p}^{t_p + \Delta t} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau\right).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces ||V||_{L^2(G)} by ||W||_{L^2(G)} by invoking a norm-invariance lemma, but V is W composed with the characteristic flow and the norm is taken over the same domain G, not over the image or preimage required by the lemma. For general G this is a misapplication; the needed composition bound is absent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a bounded composition estimate for W∘flow with constants depending on the flow Jacobian and the extension convention, or restrict the lemma to domains on which the flow is measure-preserving and identity on the domain.
issues.overall_effect: The Riesz representation step in the existence proof is not justified because the functional is not shown to be bounded.
issues.title: Boundedness of the Riesz functional is not established
issues.why_classification: The lemma can be repaired by a nontrivial but contained estimate; the main existence conclusion can survive with appropriate hypotheses or constants.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The numerical examples in Section \(\ref{sec-Tests}\) include both the 2nd-order Strang splitting and the 4th-order Ruth splitting.

issues.failure_explanation: The advertised arbitrary-order applicability includes the fourth-order Ruth scheme, which has a negative y-substep coefficient. The source's SLDG step definitions and existence/stability lemmas are formulated for positive time increments and ordered steps, with no definition or analysis for signed substeps.

failure_location.quote: The variable-separation-based dimensional splitting implementation proposed in this paper is applicable to splitting schemes of arbitrary order.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair preserving the arbitrary-order claim identified; at minimum, a repair must define and analyze the SLDG scheme for signed substeps or withdraw the Ruth/arbitrary-order applicability claim.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed coverage of fourth-order Ruth splitting, and hence the advertised arbitrary-order scope of the two-dimensional implementation, is not supported by the formal content.
issues.title: Arbitrary-order splitting claim is unsupported for negative substeps
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised regime requires new signed-step theory; the source-supported alternative excludes a central advertised splitting scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: In the displayed Strang step, the y-stage initial condition is assigned at t^{n+1/2} but the stated time interval is t^n to t^{n+1}. The general pattern remark similarly gives stage start times that omit the preceding substeps in the other direction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the stage formulas so that each substep starts and ends at the cumulative physical time determined by the previous x- and y-substeps.
issues.overall_effect: The two-dimensional splitting procedure is not correctly timed as written; time-dependent coefficients would be evaluated over wrong intervals.
issues.title: Splitting stage times are inconsistent
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of time bookkeeping; the intended splitting architecture remains unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The velocity field (-4√2 y, 2√2 x) is not a rigid rotation: its matrix square is -8I but its exponential is not orthogonal, and the flow does not return to the identity at t=π/2. Hence the stated true solution is false for the displayed PDE.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either replace the PDE by a genuine rigid-rotation velocity field with the corresponding period, or correct the reference solution for the displayed velocity field.
issues.overall_effect: The rigid-body numerical experiment does not validate the advertised periodic-return test case.
issues.title: Rigid-body test case is not rigid body rotation
issues.why_classification: The defect is local to a test example and can be repaired without affecting the main theoretical claims.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed characteristic system simultaneously imposes dx/dt=v and x(t)=x. Unless v=0, these conditions are incompatible, so the reference-solution construction is ill-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the characteristic system to the intended initial-value form, e.g. x(0)=x, v(0)=v, and integrate it to define the reference solution.
issues.overall_effect: The Landau-damping example has no valid stated exact/reference solution.
issues.title: Landau-damping characteristic system is inconsistent
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction to an example's auxiliary characteristic equations; the main analysis is unaffected.
